literal: With the earth connected, like trees they are, who, though connected with eyes, do not show kindliness.
translation: Those who possess eyes but do not look upon others with kindliness are like trees that are merely fixed to the earth.
modern: கண்களைப் பெற்றிருந்தும் பிறரிடம் இரக்கம் காட்டாதவர்கள், மண்ணோடு பொருந்தி நிற்கும் மரங்களைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of benignity or kindliness (kaṇṇōṭṭam). The author compares people who lack this quality to inanimate trees. Although they have eyes and are physically alive, their lack of empathy and kind looks makes them no better than wooden trees rooted in the soil. The word kaṇṇōṭṭam literally means the 'running of the eye' towards others in compassion; without this movement of grace, the eyes are mere physical organs, and the human is reduced to a stationary, unfeeling tree.
